content:
Sabrina James: final review request on redwood-examples PR #145 (canonical streaming + tools + structured output). This is the one we’re going to point docs + SDK READMEs at. Would love :eyes: + approvals today so we can merge and cut over links.

Sabrina James: link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-examples/pull/145

Sabrina James: last-minute things I changed since yesterday:
- renamed `function_calling/` -> `tool_calling/` everywhere (README + folder names)
- standardized filenames to `streaming_basic.*`, `tool_calling_single.*`, `tool_calling_parallel.*`, `structured_output_json_schema.*`
- updated the text to say “tool call deltas” (not “function_call chunks”) in all language READMEs
- added a short note in each language about partial tool args + aggregation (no parsing mid-stream)

Sabrina James: still open question: do we want the top-level section to be “Structured Output” or “JSON Schema”? right now README says “Structured Output (JSON Schema)”.

Ibrahim Khan: :eyes: looking now. quick skim: +1 on `tool_calling_` naming.

Ibrahim Khan: one nit: in the TS README you have “tool_call_delta events” in prose but the snippet prints `event.type === "tool_call.delta"`. can we make that consistent with canonical taxonomy? (I think we landed on `tool_call.delta` w/ dot)

Sabrina James: good catch. I’ll align the prose to `tool_call.delta` (dot) across all languages.

Dana Lo: reviewing TS folder. question: for parallel tools, can we avoid `Promise.all` without a limiter? (people will copy/paste and DDoS themselves)

Sabrina James: yep. right now it uses a simple `pLimit(4)` helper in TS, and Go uses a buffered semaphore. I can make that more obvious in TS comments + mention “cap concurrency” in the narrative.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go examples look solid. One more naming nit: the Go file is `structured_output_schema.go` but python is `structured_output_json_schema.py`. can we just make them match?

Sabrina James: yes, will rename Go to `structured_output_json_schema.go` to match.

Elliot Price: docs-side request: please keep the headings exactly “Streaming”, “Tool calling”, “Structured output” because we’re matching docs IA (and translations) off those strings. subheading can mention JSON schema.

Sabrina James: ack. I’ll keep top headings simple and add “(JSON schema)” in the subsection/intro.

Marcus Lin: security skim: thank you for the allowlist pattern + the “don’t shell out / don’t fetch arbitrary URLs” callout. One tweak: can we avoid showing tool args logging verbatim? even with examples people will paste it into prod. maybe redact to `logger.debug("tool args received")` or show selective fields.

Sabrina James: good point. I’ll change the logging lines to either omit args or show a redaction helper (`redactSecrets`) in the example.

Monica Patel: :eyes: in progress. just want to ensure this matches what we’re telling Product (tool calling terminology).

Ibrahim Khan: also: README currently says “function/tool calling” in a couple places. we should pick one. per PM-612 we’re going with “tool calling” user-facing, right?

Sabrina James: yep. I’ll remove “function” except where we’re explicitly saying “aka function calling” once in the glossary.

redwood-ci-bot: CI update for PR #145: 
- lint: PASS
- snippet-test (mock server): PASS
- linkcheck: FAIL (1 broken link)
Details: `docs/README.md` references `./tools/parallel` but folder is `./tool_calling/parallel`

Sabrina James: fixing link now.

Dana Lo: while you’re in there, can we make sure the TS install instructions don’t imply global fetch polyfill? (Node 18+ ok, but people on 16 will suffer). maybe add a note: “requires Node 18+”.

Sabrina James: added note “Node 18+” to TS README.

Mateusz Zielinski: +1 to the context timeout callout in Go. maybe mention default `context.WithTimeout` value (e.g. 60s) so people don’t hang forever.

Sabrina James: will add “recommended: 60s for demo, tune for your workload” in Go + Python.

Sabrina James: pushed a follow-up commit:
- prose/event type alignment: `tool_call.delta`
- rename Go structured output file
- add explicit concurrency cap note for parallel tools
- remove raw tool args logging, add redaction helper usage
- fix broken link

redwood-ci-bot: CI update for PR #145:
- lint: PASS
- snippet-test (mock server): PASS
- linkcheck: PASS

Ibrahim Khan: reviewed again. looks consistent w/ canonical model now. approving. :thumbsup:

Dana Lo: TS looks good w/ Node 18 note + limiter callout. approving.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go changes good. approving.

Elliot Price: headings + wording match what we need for docs. approving.

Monica Patel: thanks all. +1, please merge once Sabrina confirms no more pending nits.

Sabrina James: awesome, merging. will drop a note in #docs once it lands so we can update links in PRs 901–904.

Sabrina James: merged. next up: PR #146 snippet runner gating + scheduled staging runs. :thanks:
